scope: Case-level battle behavior for the currently declared simulator surface

status_policy.covered: A named behavior and its listed boundaries have deterministic executable evidence.
status_policy.partial: Some behavior is executable, but a named boundary or interaction remains unproved.
status_policy.open: The behavior lacks sufficient executable parity evidence or is known to be unmodeled.

baseline.name: Pokemon Showdown
baseline.champion_override_rule: Champion-specific behavior replaces the baseline only with approved Champion evidence.

cases.behavior: Mapped roster types and unboosted Speed agree with runtime stats; supported Eternal Flower aliases preserve species identity.
cases.oracle: Pinned Champions species baseline plus engine starting-stat contract; not battle ordering or official legality.
cases.known_gap: All item/ability/field combinations, Mega alias transitions and in-game Champions confirmation remain unproved.

cases.behavior: A Pokemon keeps its stable identity when active and bench positions change.
cases.oracle: Local stable-key contract validated across replacement snapshots.

cases.behavior: Held-item ownership remains attached to the same stable Pokemon through switches and replacements.
cases.oracle: Local roster and item continuity contract.

cases.behavior: A damaging move can KO its target and then KO its user by recoil before replacements.
cases.oracle: Pokemon Showdown recoil lifecycle baseline.
cases.known_gap: The existing fixture proves recoil cleanup but does not yet assert both sides replacing from the same attack.

cases.behavior: Multiple residual KOs resolve before replacement decisions without losing identity or source attribution.
cases.oracle: Pokemon Showdown residual event queue.
cases.known_gap: Both-side poison KOs now have a 100-seed replacement fixture; mixed residual sources and full attribution remain unproved.

cases.behavior: Two fainted slots on one side receive distinct legal replacements in the correct order.
cases.oracle: Pokemon Showdown switch request and replacement queue.
cases.known_gap: Replacement selection is engine-policy driven and has no two-slot lifecycle fixture.

cases.behavior: Both sides can replace fainted Pokemon from one resolved event without side-order corruption.
cases.oracle: Pokemon Showdown simultaneous switch request behavior.
cases.known_gap: Both fields now populate before entry abilities; mutual Intimidate passes 100 seeds. Wider entry-effect and multi-slot ordering still needs differential proof.

cases.behavior: Entry abilities after simultaneous replacements resolve using the correct ordering rules.
cases.oracle: Pokemon Showdown event ordering baseline.
cases.known_gap: Mutual Intimidate and side-swapped weather clashes with/without Trick Room are tested. Equal-Speed entry ordering and reactive abilities still need committed differential fixtures.

cases.behavior: Regenerator restores one third base max HP, rounded down, after a successful switch-out.
cases.oracle: https://github.com/smogon/pokemon-showdown/blob/master/data/abilities.ts

cases.behavior: Regenerator does not activate when no legal replacement exists.
cases.oracle: Pokemon Showdown onSwitchOut event semantics.

cases.behavior: Regenerator activates after a successful U-turn, Volt Switch, or Flip Turn pivot.
cases.oracle: Pokemon Showdown self-switch plus onSwitchOut event semantics.
cases.known_gap: The shared switch hook is covered, but no dedicated damaging-pivot Regenerator fixture asserts all three moves.

cases.behavior: Volatile state and stat stages reset on switch while major status and HP remain attached to the Pokemon.
cases.oracle: Pokemon Showdown switch lifecycle baseline.
cases.known_gap: Several resets are source-contract tests rather than one executable leave-and-return fixture.

cases.behavior: Move priority resolves before effective Speed.
cases.oracle: Pokemon Showdown action ordering baseline.

cases.behavior: Trick Room reverses effective Speed only inside the same priority bracket.
cases.oracle: Pokemon Showdown Trick Room ordering baseline.

cases.behavior: Exact effective-Speed ties use deterministic seeded RNG.
cases.oracle: Local deterministic replay contract aligned to Showdown random tie breaking.

cases.behavior: Three or four actions in the same priority and effective-Speed bracket receive one stable seeded random order.
cases.oracle: Pokemon Showdown speed-sort random tie grouping.

cases.behavior: A team played against an identical copy has no material player-side or opponent-side advantage across independent seed families.
cases.oracle: Metamorphic mirror-match fairness invariant plus Pokemon Showdown event-order baseline.
cases.known_gap: Sequential replacement Intimidate was causal and is fixed locally. Broader multi-team side symmetry and explicit bring-four parity remain release gates.

cases.behavior: Battle stat stages clamp at minus six and plus six.
cases.oracle: Pokemon Showdown boost stage baseline.

cases.behavior: Accuracy succeeds only when the random roll is strictly below the effective threshold.
cases.oracle: https://github.com/smogon/pokemon-showdown/blob/master/sim/battle.ts

cases.behavior: A standard single-target damaging move consumes one accuracy roll.
cases.oracle: Pokemon Showdown hitStepAccuracy.
cases.known_gap: The duplicate engine check was removed, but an injected RNG call-count fixture is still needed.

cases.behavior: Targeted status moves use their Showdown-mirrored accuracy and consume the roll at the correct point in target resolution.
cases.oracle: Pokemon Showdown status-move hit-step ordering.
cases.known_gap: Common hit and miss paths exist, but one fixture does not yet prove immunity, reflection, Substitute, and accuracy-roll ordering together.

cases.behavior: A spread move performs an independent accuracy check for each target.
cases.oracle: https://github.com/smogon/pokemon-showdown/blob/master/sim/battle-actions.ts

cases.behavior: Type and move immunities are resolved before consuming a target accuracy roll.
cases.oracle: Pokemon Showdown trySpreadMoveHit step ordering.
cases.known_gap: A mixed-target Earth Eater spread fixture is proved; dedicated type-immunity and single-target RNG-consumption fixtures remain.

cases.behavior: No Guard bypasses accuracy for only the targets where attacker or target supplies it.
cases.oracle: Pokemon Showdown ModifyAccuracy and Accuracy events per target.
cases.known_gap: Single-target No Guard is covered; mixed spread targets are not.

cases.behavior: A later single-target action retargets when its intended opponent has already fainted.
cases.oracle: Pokemon Showdown doubles retargeting baseline.

cases.behavior: Follow Me and Rage Powder redirect eligible single-target moves with documented bypasses.
cases.oracle: Pokemon Showdown redirection baseline.

cases.behavior: Ally Switch, redirection, Protect, and a fainted slot compose without stale target references.
cases.oracle: Pokemon Showdown target-location semantics.
cases.known_gap: No deterministic interaction fixture covers this cross-product.

cases.behavior: Wide Guard blocks eligible spread attacks without changing unrelated target resolution.
cases.oracle: Pokemon Showdown Wide Guard baseline.
cases.known_gap: Wide Guard basics are covered, but mixed per-target protection and accuracy ordering is not.

cases.behavior: Weather, abilities, status, seeds, delayed healing, items, terrain, and field expiry use the correct end-of-turn order.
cases.oracle: Pokemon Showdown residual event priorities and suborders.
cases.known_gap: Eight side-swapped Leftovers/Toxic probes cover full HP and ticks through five, including rounding before multiplication. Effects still use fixed family loops; mixed recovery, Heal Block expiry, lethal residual boundaries and full queue parity remain unproved.

cases.behavior: Same-priority residual effects use the correct effective-Speed and tie ordering.
cases.oracle: Pokemon Showdown residual event sorting.
cases.known_gap: Residual loops currently use side/slot array order.

cases.behavior: Wish heals the Pokemon occupying the original slot rather than following the original user identity.
cases.oracle: Pokemon Showdown Wish slot-condition semantics.

cases.behavior: Leech Seed damage and healing keep correct source/slot behavior through switches and faints.
cases.oracle: Pokemon Showdown Leech Seed volatile semantics.
cases.known_gap: Ordinary drain is covered; source and recipient lifecycle boundaries are not.

cases.behavior: Perish Song reaching zero on multiple Pokemon resolves all faints and the winner correctly.
cases.oracle: Pokemon Showdown Perish Song residual ordering.
cases.known_gap: Four-turn reference probes cover countdown, recast and named immunity gates; two-wave terminal winner/faint-order with/without Trick Room and Phantom Force/No Guard controls also pass. Tied residual speeds, voluntary switch/re-entry and other semi-invulnerability remain unproved. Replacement choices differ by policy; matching counts and legal membership do not prove identical tactical continuation.

cases.behavior: PP consumption, Pressure, move exhaustion, and Struggle are modeled together.
cases.oracle: Pokemon Showdown move-slot and Pressure behavior.

cases.behavior: Spite and Eerie Spell respect Substitute bypass and relevant defensive or secondary-effect gates.
cases.oracle: Pinned pokemon-showdown 0.11.11 gen9championsdoublescustomgame synthetic probes, not Champions legality approval.
cases.known_gap: Slot-1 and ally targeting, general reflection recursion, item suppression, exact random damage and complete-game/UI parity are not established by these bounded probes.

cases.behavior: Supported forced Struggle paths apply fixed damage, recoil, and faint cleanup.
cases.oracle: Current project Struggle contract pending full PP integration.

cases.behavior: Mega, stance, and supported Tera state persist or reset correctly through switching.
cases.oracle: Pokemon Showdown form and terastallization lifecycle baseline plus approved Champion overrides.
cases.known_gap: The individual systems are covered, but one lifecycle suite does not prove every supported transformation through switching.

cases.behavior: Every import-accepted move, ability, item, species, and form has executable mechanics parity evidence.
cases.oracle: Generated Showdown inventory plus executable differential fixtures.
cases.known_gap: Import legality is broader than verified battle behavior.

cases.behavior: Hospitality heals an eligible ally on either side.
cases.oracle: Pokemon Showdown Hospitality onStart baseline.

cases.behavior: Battle participants match the bring-four roster reported in the exported log.
cases.oracle: Official VGC selected-four requirement; independent old-engine explicit-selection differential and roster/export consistency contract.

cases.behavior: Thousand Arrows hits Flying targets and applies grounding.
cases.oracle: Pokemon Showdown Thousand Arrows immunity and grounding baseline.
cases.known_gap: Listed synthetic boundaries pass; Air Balloon, Gravity, semi-invulnerable states and approved Champion legality remain unproven.

cases.behavior: Positive-priority multi-hit attacks obey side ability, Quick Guard and Psychic Terrain protection.
cases.oracle: Pokemon Showdown priority protection baseline; synthetic Gale Wings Dual Wingbeat fixtures.
cases.known_gap: Protection boundaries pass locally; broader multi-hit accuracy, redirection and per-hit ability parity are not established.

cases.behavior: Tailwind changes the order of remaining moves during the same turn.
cases.oracle: pokemon-showdown@0.11.11 Champions custom doubles; tailwind-midturn-speed reference probe.
cases.known_gap: Pinned synthetic doubles probes agree for the listed boundaries. Other arbitrary mid-turn Speed or priority changes, exact ties after a change, full-game/UI parity and official Champions confirmation remain unproved. No production promotion.

cases.behavior: Seismic Toss deals level-based damage to a valid nonimmune target.
cases.oracle: pokemon-showdown@0.11.11 Champions custom doubles; seismic-toss-fixed-damage reference probe.
cases.known_gap: Ten isolated pinned doubles probes agree; additional preview and HP-application tests are local only. Other fixed-damage moves, arbitrary ability/item combinations, full-game/UI parity and official Champions confirmation remain unproved.

cases.behavior: Growl and Leer lower the relevant stats of unprotected opposing targets.
cases.oracle: pokemon-showdown@0.11.11 Champions custom doubles; fixed-damage and Earthquake reference probes.
cases.known_gap: Pinned synthetic doubles probes agree for the listed boundaries. The broader stat-stage move, ability and item inventory, imported full games, UI parity and official Champions confirmation remain unproved.

cases.behavior: Regulation M-B differences from Showdown baseline are backed by approved Champion evidence and tests.
cases.oracle: Approved official or captured Pokemon Champions evidence.
cases.known_gap: Authoritative Regulation M-B evidence remains incomplete.
